issues.title: Zero-dim VectorType with nil SubType still panics when unmarshaled into *any
issues.verdictReason: Reproduced directly: unmarshalVector(VectorType{}, []byte{}, &dst) with dst any panics with a nil-pointer dereference because t.Kind()==reflect.Interface unconditionally calls info.Zero(), which calls v.SubType.NewWithError() on a nil SubType interface (marshal.go:2045) regardless of Dimensions==0; the new dimension bound only guards the elemMin computation, not this path, and the new test TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType only exercises a *[]float64 destination.
issues.scopeReason: The PR's own stated goal is to stop unmarshalVector from crashing the Scan goroutine on attacker/peer-controlled input, and explicitly claims (via a new test and comment) that zero-dimension vectors with a nil SubType are now safe; this residual panic on the *any path undermines that exact claim and belongs in the same fix.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType and the guard comment say a zero VectorType with a nil SubType is safe at zero dimensions. That only holds for a concrete-slice destination: with an *any destination, unmarshalVector still calls info.Zero(), which dereferences the nil SubType.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-added-diff-2026-10-09/tidepool/revi: TestUnmarshalVectorZeroDimensionsDoesNotTouchSubType and the guard comment say a zero VectorType with a nil SubType is safe at zero dimensions. issues.title: getCassandraLongType's custom-name change silently alters TypeInfo for all unrecognized…
issues.verdictReason: getCassandraLongType is the general recursive class-name parser used for list/set/map elems, tuple fields, UDT fields, and vector subtypes (helpers.go:211-277); the new branch at helpers.go:280-284 applies to every 'basic type' fallthrough, not just vector elements, so TypeInfo.Custom() (previously empty string) and String() (previously 'custom()') now report the full class name everywhere an unrecognized type appears, not only inside vectors.
issues.scopeReason: The behavior change is new code added by this PR's diff to helpers.go, and its blast radius (all metadata consumers of TypeInfo) is wider than the PR describes (only vector error messages), so it is this PR's responsibility to document or narrow.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: getCassandraLongType now returns NativeType with `custom` set to the full class name for every unrecognised type, not only vector elements. That changes the public TypeInfo.Custom() and String() output for collection, tuple, UDT and vector-subtype metadata across the driver, and neither the commit nor the PR body calls it a contract change.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-added-diff-2026-10-09/tidepool/revi: getCassandraLongType now returns NativeType with `custom` set to the full class name for every unrecognised type, not only vector elements. issues.verdictReason: CONTRIBUTING.md:25 requires notable behaviour changes to be documented in CHANGELOG.md and functional changes in godoc; this repo has no CHANGELOG.md file at all, and no exported godoc (e.g. on VectorType, NativeType.Custom/String, or Unmarshal) was updated to describe the new dimension-bound rejection or the unknown-type-name preservation, even though both are real behaviour changes a caller could observe.
issues.scopeReason: The undocumented behaviour changes are exactly what this PR introduces.

issues.title: 'Payload with a trailing byte' test mislabels a malformed payload as well-formed
issues.verdictReason: The subtest feeds a 13-byte payload to a 3-dimension, 4-byte-fixed int vector (not evenly divisible by 3) and asserts success under TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads's banner that 'a vector of N elements is never encoded in fewer than N bytes' -- 13 bytes is not a valid encoding of 3 int32s; the generic (non-float-fast-path) decode loop derives elemSize via integer division (len(data)/Dimensions) and never checks for leftover bytes, so it silently accepts it while the float32/float64 fast paths would reject the same mismatch outright. This looseness itself predates the PR and is the PR body's explicitly out-of-scope issue (#1086), so the test is accurately pinning current behaviour, but its 'well-formed' framing is inaccurate.
issues.scopeReason: The test and its misleading framing are new in this PR, even though the underlying trailing-bytes leniency is pre-existing and was explicitly declared out of scope by the PR author.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads includes a 'payload with a trailing byte' case: a 13-byte int vector with 3 dimensions. That payload is malformed, yet the test asserts it decodes without error. The float fast paths reject any length other than Dimensions*size.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-added-diff-2026-10-09/tidepool/revi: TestUnmarshalVectorAcceptsWellFormedPayloads includes a 'payload with a trailing byte' case: a 13-byte int vector with 3 dimensions. That payload is malformed, yet the test asserts it decodes without error. The float fast paths reject any length other than Dimensions*size.

issues.title: Allocation-regression test uses process-wide TotalAlloc, vulnerable to…
issues.verdictReason: TestUnmarshalVectorRejectsNestedCountBeforeAllocating reads runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc (process-wide) around the call under test; its own comment notes it deliberately avoids t.Parallel() with sibling subtests in the same file, but that does not stop allocations from unrelated goroutines already running in the process (GC workers, finalizers, other packages' init/background work) from being counted in TotalAlloc, which is a real if generally low-probability source of flakiness for this specific assertion style.
issues.scopeReason: This test is new in this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The allocation-regression test uses process-wide TotalAlloc and can be polluted by allocations from unrelated background goroutines.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-added-diff-2026-10-09/tidepool/revi: The allocation-regression test uses process-wide TotalAlloc and can be polluted by allocations from unrelated background goroutines.
